cutout.alt: Chris Woods, MSN, APRN, FNP-C, AGACNP-BC, smiling with a stethoscope

figures.alt: Chart of five common screening tests and what each checks: metabolic panel for kidneys, liver, salts, and sugar; cholesterol for blood fats; A1c for three-month average sugar; TSH for the thyroid; CBC for red cells, white cells, and platelets.
figures.caption: Five common screening tests and the question each one answers.

figures.alt: Two columns comparing the basic metabolic panel with 8 tests and the comprehensive metabolic panel, which adds 6 liver and protein tests.
figures.caption: The CMP is the BMP plus liver and protein numbers.

figures.alt: Lipid panel targets for most adults: total cholesterol under 200, LDL under 100, HDL 40 or more for men and 50 or more for women, triglycerides under 150, all in milligrams per deciliter.
figures.caption: Common targets for most adults. Your own goal depends on your full risk.

figures.alt: A1c range bar: below 5.7 percent normal, 5.7 to 6.4 percent prediabetes, 6.5 percent or higher diabetes.
figures.caption: A1c ranges. Diabetes is confirmed with two tests.

figures.alt: Diagram of the brain sending TSH to the thyroid. High TSH usually means an underactive thyroid. Low TSH usually means an overactive thyroid.
figures.caption: TSH runs backward: high usually means slow, low usually means fast.

figures.alt: Three columns: red blood cells deliver oxygen, white blood cells fight germs, platelets plug leaks.
figures.caption: The CBC counts the delivery crew, the defense crew, and the repair crew.

figures.alt: Screening schedule for most adults: cholesterol every 4 to 6 years from about age 20, sugar every 3 years from 35 if carrying extra weight, hepatitis C once from 18 to 79, HIV at least once from 15 to 65.
figures.caption: A plain starting schedule. Risk factors and symptoms move it earlier.

stickers: An H is a nudge, not a verdict

figures.alt: Bell curve showing the middle 95 percent of healthy people as the normal range, with 1 in 20 healthy people landing just outside it.
figures.caption: 1 in 20 healthy people lands outside the range on any single test.
